prompt:
A photograph taken down the length of the fold-out packing bench in the back of a scene-of-crime van, the whole bench in the frame with the roller door at the far end.

Three exhibits have just been sealed at this bench and stand along it, each in its own sealed bag with its own printed reference label facing the camera. The references and their contents are, word for word:
        JB/1 .... flat-blade screwdriver, 250 mm
        JB/2 .... left glove, wet with blood
        JB/3 .... mobile telephone, switched on

This force keeps three kinds of packaging on the bench and the unused stock of all three sits at the far end where the officer can reach it: brown kraft sacks, clear plastic bags, and silver-foil pouches. Rigid tubes are kept in the same rack.

Which of those an exhibit goes into is a matter of what the exhibit is, and this officer has packed the three of them the way the force's own packaging policy requires. Work out for yourself what each one had to go into -- I am deliberately not telling you which bag any exhibit ended up in, and I am not telling you what goes round anything inside a bag.

The label of each bag has to be legible from the camera and its own exhibit reference has to be on it. Nothing on the bench and nothing on the van wall states the packaging policy or names a material for an exhibit.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show sealed exhibit bags standing on a bench with reference labels on them? A photograph, a document mockup or an illustration ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image shows a blank card that just states an answer, or shows nothing of the kind at all. Answer yes or no only.
